title: Futuro Simple — Practice
description: Authored B1 practice set for the simple future: -é endings on the infinitive, the irregular stems (shared with the conditional), and the future of conjecture.

lessons.summary: The simple future (futuro simple) says what will happen. Form it by adding -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án to the whole infinitive — the endings are the same for -ar, -er and -ir verbs: hablaré, comerás, viviremos. Every form except nosotros carries a written accent. A dozen verbs use an irregular stem instead of the infinitive — the same stems as the conditional: tener → tendré, poner → pondré, salir → saldré, venir → vendré, poder → podré, saber → sabré, querer → querré, haber → habré (impersonal habrá), hacer → haré, decir → diré, valer → valdré, caber → cabré. The future is also used for conjecture about the present — '¿Qué hora será?' means 'I wonder what time it is', and 'Serán las tres' means 'It must be about three'. In speech, 'ir a + infinitive' (voy a llamar) often replaces the simple future for near plans.

examples.spanish: El año que viene viviremos en España.
examples.english: Next year we'll live in Spain.
I won't have time this week.
I wonder what time it is.
examples.note: future of conjecture, not a prediction

examples.spanish: Habrá mucha gente en la fiesta.
examples.english: There'll be a lot of people at the party.

items.explanation: Add -é to the full infinitive: hablar + é = hablaré.
comer + ás = comerás. The endings are identical for -ar, -er and -ir verbs.
vivir + emos = viviremos — the only form without a written accent.
hablar + án = hablarán.
ser is regular in the future: ser + á = será.
tener uses the irregular stem 'tendr-': tendré.
hacer uses the shortened stem 'har-': haré (not 'haceré').
decir uses the shortened stem 'dir-': dirá.
poder drops the -e- of the infinitive: 'podr-' + emos = podremos.
salir replaces the -i- with -d-: 'saldr-' + án = saldrán.
venir → 'vendr-': vendrás.
saber drops the -e-: 'sabr-' + é = sabré.
poner → 'pondr-': pondrá.
querer drops the -e- and keeps the double r: 'querr-' + é = querré.
hay → habrá. Impersonal haber stays singular even with a plural noun: 'Habrá muchas personas'.
llamar + é = llamaré.

items.prompt: El año que viene ___ en España. (vivir, nosotros)
items.promptEnglish: Next year we'll live in Spain.
items.explanation: vivir + emos = viviremos.

items.promptEnglish: I won't have time this week.
items.explanation: Irregular stem tendr-: tendré.

items.prompt: ¿Qué hora ___? (ser — 'I wonder what time it is')
items.promptEnglish: I wonder what time it is.
items.explanation: The future also expresses conjecture about the present: '¿Qué hora será?' = 'I wonder what time it is.'
Future of conjecture, plural subject: estarán.

items.promptEnglish: What will you do this weekend?
items.explanation: hacer → har-: harás.

items.prompt: Which is the future of hacer ('I will do it')? ___ lo.
items.explanation: hacer has the irregular stem har-, so 'haceré' does not exist.

items.prompt: 'It must be about three o'clock.' → ___ las tres.
items.promptEnglish: It must be about three o'clock.
items.explanation: The future marks a guess about the present. 'Son las tres' states the time as a fact.

items.prompt: Which one is the simple future ('I will go')?
items.explanation: Both talk about the future, but the simple future is the one-word form: iré. 'Voy a ir' is ir a + infinitive.

items.prompt: Into the simple future: "Voy a estudiar" → "___" (I will study).
items.explanation: ir a + infinitive → simple future: estudiar + é = estudiaré.

items.prompt: Into the simple future: "Comemos a las ocho" → "___ a las ocho" (we will eat at eight).
items.explanation: comer + emos = comeremos.

items.prompt: Escribe una frase en futuro simple sobre algo que harás el año que viene.
items.promptEnglish: Write a simple-future sentence about something you'll do next year.
items.guidance: Must be grammatical Spanish using a simple future form (infinitive or irregular stem + -é/-ás/-á/-emos/-án), e.g. 'El año que viene aprenderé a cocinar.' Mark incorrect if it uses 'ir a + infinitive' (voy a aprender), the conditional (aprendería), or the present instead of the simple future.
items.sampleAnswer: El año que viene viajaré a Argentina y visitaré a mi familia.
items.explanation: The simple future adds -é/-ás/-á/-emos/-án to the infinitive.
